thread:
sam: Heads up — noticed a ~22% p50 regression on Mixtral-8k runs after the kernel-selector tuning yesterday. trace + quick numbers below.

anya: Hmm, which selector change exactly? the auto-fallback to the generic matmul?

sam: Yeah — the selector moved Mixtral -> int8_matmul_v2 on A100s for short seqs. Logs:

```
KERNEL_SELECT: model=mixtral-8k, seq=512, selected=int8_matmul_v2, fallback=cuBLAS
PERF: p50=31ms (baseline 25ms)
```

kevin: Can you paste profiler counters (l2_misses, bank_conflicts, gld/gst)?

sam: Quick snippet from perf tool: 

```
samples: 120k
l2_read_hits: 54%
l2_read_misses: 46%
bank_conflicts: high
warp_stalls_mem: 18%
mem_ops_extra: observed on kv gather step
```

kevin: That looks like extra memory chatter during KV fetches. Could be RoPE precompute layout mismatch causing uncoalesced loads.

jess: Also note Mixtral uses head_dim=128 with scaled RoPE, while our int8 kernel was optimized for head_dim=64 contiguous blocks. If the kernel assumes 64-byte lanes it will thrash for 128.

anya: Proposal: adaptive-kv-tiering — keep recent/prefix tokens in fp16 (hot tier) and quantize older tokens to int8 (cold tier). This reduces memory and avoids kernel fallback for hot cache entries.

kevin: Nice. Combine that with batch-shaping: break initial tokens into small "starter" batches so the kernel picks the small-seq optimized path, then coalesce midstream tokens into bigger batches for throughput. We saw 12% cost drop on llama-70b with similar shaping.

perf-bot: queued profile job #4872 for adaptive-kv-tiering prototype.

sam: Repro command for local test: 

```
./run_inference --model mixtral-8k --seq 1024 --kernel-selector auto \
  --kv-precision fp16,int8:threshold=256 --batch-shape adaptive
```

anya: Also a small guard in the kernel selector could avoid the regression: check RoPE scale & head_dim before allowing int8_matmul_v2. Patch idea:

```
// in selector
if (model.head_dim % 128 == 0 && seq_len > 512) {
  prefer_rope_scaled_kernel();
}
```

kevin: I'll run A/B on dedicated pool (pool-dedicated-2). Note: eviction policy interacts — if prefix cache evicts too aggressively we repeatedly recompute and the selector flips kernels. For the test, bump prefix TTL to 2000 tokens.

sam: After TTL bump: p50 moved to 26ms (baseline 25ms), memory +6%, regression mostly mitigated.

jess: Sounds promising. For adaptive-kv-tiering we need config knobs: tier1_precision, tier2_precision, ttl_tokens, quant_algo. I'll draft a short RFC.

anya: I'll sketch config and expected tradeoffs. Quick recommended defaults: tier1=fp16 (recent 512 tokens), tier2=int8 (older), quant_algo=per-channel-minmax, ttl_tokens=2000.

kevin: Running overnight runs now. Will include metrics: p50, p95, token-thruput, mem-footprint, kernel-switch-rate.

perf-bot: run #4872 complete (18h). Summary:
- mixed workload: memory footprint -28% vs baseline
- p50 improved 8% vs baseline after adaptive tiers + batch shaping
- kernel-switch events reduced by 67%

jess: Nice win. Next: add unit perf tests to catch selector regressions. I'll add a prompt set that highlights short-seq QoS and RoPE-sensitive patterns.

sam: I've created a draft RFC: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/123 — includes prototype config and telemetry events. Please review and leave comments. :thumbsup:

anya: +1. Also log a follow-up issue to evaluate per-head precision (experiment: quantize only low-variance heads to int8). That might buy extra memory without hurting quality.

kevin: I'll post the overnight numbers in the morning with per-kernel flame graphs and bank-conflict heatmaps.

perf-bot: tagging relevant tests: runtime-selector, kv-tiering, rope-scaling, batch-shape.

sam: Great work team. Plan: canary deploy adaptive-kv-tiering + selector guard on dedicated pool next week, monitor kernel-switch-rate and p95.

jess: I'll prepare the canary runbook and rollback criteria.

kevin: On it.
